14790897/sleep-secret.body:
# Sleep Recording Analysis

Record overnight, split sounds into categories such as snoring, breathing, coughing, and sleep talk, all locally on your phone, and get a timeline and statistics in the morning.

**By default, audio never leaves the device.** There is no account and no server, so you can install and use it right away. All analysis happens on the phone.

The only exception is if **you yourself** set up 坚果云 (Jianguoyun) / WebDAV on the Export Data page. After that, each night's recording is uploaded to a cloud drive **under your own name**. This project has no server of its own, and never will.

**Documentation site**: <https://mygithub.sixiangjia.de/sleep-secret/> ([Usage Guide](https://mygithub.sixiangjia.de/sleep-secret/guide/) · [Understanding the Report](https://mygithub.sixiangjia.de/sleep-secret/report/) · [Data & Privacy](https://mygithub.sixiangjia.de/sleep-secret/privacy/))

## Install on your phone

- **F-Droid (recommended)**: <https://f-droid.org/packages/com.sleepsecret.sleep_secret/>. The F-Droid and GitHub builds **use the same signing key**, so they can be installed over each other without losing data. However, F-Droid index updates are delayed, so its version may lag behind Releases by a few days.
- **GitHub Releases**: Go to [Releases](https://github.com/14790897/sleep-secret/releases) and download the latest
`app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` (the architecture used by most phones), then install it directly. Apart from F-Droid, the app is not listed on any other app store. Installing from GitHub requires allowing “Install unknown apps.”

The first time you open the app, grant the **Recording** and **Notification** permissions. On systems such as Xiaomi and Huawei, you also need to set the battery policy to “No restrictions,” allow auto-start, and lock the app in recent tasks. Otherwise, the system may kill the overnight recording, and you will only get an empty report in the morning.

## What it does

Tap once before bed to start, and tap again the next morning to stop. That night's report will **open automatically**.

(If you accidentally start and immediately stop, or the analyzed duration is under 10 seconds, the app first asks “keep or delete?” instead of quietly leaving an empty record. For a deliberate microphone test of about 10 seconds, choose “keep.”)

- **Overnight sound timeline**: when sound occurred, what kind it was, and how long it lasted
- **Snore index**: the percentage of the analysis duration spent snoring, for comparing across nights
- **Category and hourly distribution**: which hours were the noisiest
- **Event details**: the time, category, and confidence of each event. Snoring events can also be tapped to listen.

The nine recognized categories: **snoring / breathing / coughing and throat-clearing / sneezing / human speech (sleep talk) / body movement and bed creaking / ambient noise / device noise / …**

# Shanggan (上岸)

**An civil-service exam practice app that fits 200,000 real exam questions on your phone. Works offline, has no ads, and explanations don't require a membership.**

An offline practice tool for civil service exams, public institution recruitment, and the Three-Support-One-Assistance program (三支一扶), covering 行测 (Administrative Aptitude Test) / 职测 (Occupational Aptitude Test) / 公基 (Public Basic Knowledge) / 申论 (Essay Writing) / 综应 (Comprehensive Application). Question banks, explanations, and formula images are all bundled in the installation package and run on local SQLite on the phone, so you can practice without a network connection.

The question sources are two sets: Fenbi (粉笔) with 166,000 questions, including official difficulty ratings and site-wide correct rates, and Huatu (华图) with 33,000 real exam papers, imported according to the official exam paper structure, with an official module tree and five difficulty levels.

## What is this

Civil-service exam apps on the market fall roughly into two types. Big-company products have comprehensive question banks but require an internet connection, show ads, and split explanations between free and paid membership. Personally curated question banks have good content but are only PDFs and cloud-drive links that can't be practiced interactively: there is no wrong-answer notebook and no statistics, and flipping through PDFs on a phone to do five hundred questions is torture.

The gap in between is obvious: **a tool you can actually practice with, with complete content, offline, and free of commercial interference**.

Technically it isn't hard. The difficult parts are three things, and most of this project's engineering effort went into them:

1. How to fit two hundred thousand questions into one installation package while keeping WebView opening without lag
2. How to keep updates to tens of MB instead of re-downloading 600 MB as questions keep being added
3. How to make question quality acceptable. Mismatched answers and explanations, lost images, and swallowed formulas are more discouraging than a small quantity

Longado/ontopoc.description: Ontology tool for MCP / Claude: draft, check, and confirm ontologies from business data. Schema work ahead of a knowledge graph or semantic layer.
Longado/ontopoc.body:
OntoPoc is still in development and has no users beyond its author. The current main line is a team application (page root `/`): upload spreadsheets or connect read-only to PostgreSQL / MySQL, build datasets and pipelines, and create object types, relationships, views, behaviors, and derived properties from the data. Each item is checked by code against the data, confirmed by another builder, and the data version at the time of confirmation is recorded. Q&A, dashboards, and agents use only confirmed definitions. When the data changes, affected definitions return to “needs review,” and questions that depend on them are refused, with the item named and the person who can confirm it identified.

## Team application

| Section | What it does |
|---|---|
| Accounts and permissions | Local accounts with three roles (admin, builder, viewer), server-side sessions. Admins can restrict people by object type, restrict people by row (allowlist only), and keep a column's values from being sent to the model |
| Data | Datasets: upload CSV / Excel, update or overwrite by primary key, each time creating a new version. Data sources: read-only connections to PostgreSQL and MySQL, with optional certificate verification. Scheduling: pull data or run pipelines on a timer, hourly or daily |
| Pipelines | Operators such as filter, join, group-and-aggregate, deduplicate, and computed columns; expression editor. AI steps ask the model row by row. Columns they write can only be used as primary keys or code meanings after sample review and confirmation by another builder |
| Ontology | Object types (properties, primary keys, meanings of code columns); relationships (checks how many rows are linked and whether the declared cardinality holds); views (e.g., “valid orders”); behaviors (parameters, submission conditions, and writes to data only after approval); derived properties (a formula over the same row, or aggregates across a relationship) |
| Confirmation | Proposed → code check → confirmation by another builder. With only one builder, confirmation is automatic and recorded. Confirmation stores the data version and anchor. After a new version is uploaded, items are re-checked; those that no longer match return to “needs review,” and anything that reads them goes with them, with the reason stated (data changed, definition changed, or upstream stale). Several items arising from one upload can be confirmed together on one page |
| Q&A | Scope covers only confirmed types this person can see. If a question mentions an unconfirmed or needs-review definition, it is refused first, with the reason given, without asking the model. The model sees structure, meanings, and values of low-cardinality columns, but not row data, and writes a structured query. The code executes it and checks the definitions used. Supports excluding a meaning (“not canceled”) and top or bottom N. Answers are stored with their definitions, confirmer, and data version |
| Use | Object browsing, dashboards, MCP tools for agents (uses personal tokens, read-only by default), relationship graph and lineage graph (colored by “data changed / definition changed / previous step stale / further upstream stale”) |

The early interface organized around “a single run” is still at `legacy.html`; see [Early interface](#早期界面按运行建模) below.

Longado/shifu.description: A macOS workspace for your coding agents. Live status, split terminals, and sessions that keep running.
Longado/shifu.body:
Once you have many agents, you don't have to switch between terminals one by one: Shifu lines up the sessions that need your attention together.

**Each vendor's terminal is kept as-is** · **keeps running after the window is closed** · **tasks and layouts are saved locally**

## What it is

Shifu puts Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, CodeBuddy and Antigravity into a single macOS window. The left side organizes sessions by project and task, showing who is running, who is waiting for approval, and who is waiting for your reply; the right side is each agent's own terminal, where you can drag tabs and split them left/right or up/down.

Sessions are managed by a separate tmux server; the desktop app only handles display and operation. Closing or reopening the window does not end the agents; when you return, tasks and split layouts are restored. The command line can also be used on its own. See the [architecture notes](https://github.com/Longado/shifu/blob/HEAD/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the design.

> **Early version.** Currently mainly used on Apple Silicon Macs. You can download the Apple Silicon pre-release package or build from source; the app is not yet notarized. By default Shifu launches Claude, Codex, CodeBuddy and Kimi in no-confirmation mode, so they won't ask for permission item by item when modifying files or running commands. Before installing, please read the [startup notes](#快速开始) and [known issues](#已知问题).

## How it works

| When you... | It will... |
|---|---|
| Create a task, choosing an agent, directory and model | Start a session in a dedicated tmux server and receive that agent's status |
| The agent stops to wait for approval or a reply | Mark the status in the sidebar and move it to the top under "Waiting for you" |
| Press ⌘J, or click a waiting session | Jump to the corresponding task and activate the original terminal |
| Drag a tab, or right-click to choose a split direction | Place terminals side by side or stacked, keeping each one's interaction method |
| Click a file path in the terminal | Open the file beside the conversation; Markdown can be edited and saved directly |
| Close Shifu and reopen it | Agents keep running, and tasks and split layouts are restored |

The source adds a "Daily Analysis" resident session, which can manually summarize project progress and blockers. Security, cloud machine spending and agent usage only read sources the user configures themselves, and scheduled tasks are configured separately. The standalone remote page groups by real Task, supports searching tasks and sessions, and keeps keyboard focus and collapsed state after refresh. Ordinary stopped sessions show "Waiting for input", and the page can be collapsed while keeping the connection. Task grouping requires the remote connection service to be updated at the same time; old remotes can still use the ungrouped list. Terminal links avoid opening twice on a single click. Computer operation supports an optional strict background mode that only allows read-only operations and accessibility text assignment, rejecting clicks, key presses and foreground fallback. Existing pre-release download packages do not include these source increments. [Changelog](https://github.com/Longado/shifu/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md).

# TG Persona · Telegram Persona Clone

## Features

Each account's session is stored independently, so no re-login is needed after a restart.

Wolido/async-subagent-isolation.description: Fix context rot & pollution in long AI agent sessions. Subagents run in isolated processes — main agent stays read-only. Context isolation via process isolation.
Wolido/async-subagent-isolation.body:
Is your AI agent “forgetting” things, producing worse output, or even modifying files on its own after a long session? These are typical symptoms of context explosion, context rot, and context pollution. **async-subagent-isolation** is an extension for [Pi Agent](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) and the **asynchronous evolution** of [subagent-isolation](https://github.com/Wolido/subagent-isolation) (the synchronous version). It solves these problems with subagent process isolation.

The core constraint is unchanged: **the main agent may not touch code**. It has no `write`, no `edit`, and no `bash`. It has only four read-only tools, `read`, `grep`, `find`, and `ls`, plus one `subagent` delegation tool. All work that modifies files, runs commands, or executes logic is handed to subagents. Two core selling points follow from this. First, **skill-level prompt isolation**: each subagent runs in its own `pi` process, with its own agent definition file (such as `coder.md`) and skill allowlist. It does not inherit the main agent's prompts or skills, so none of the main agent's skills get in. Second, a **division-of-labor model**: the main agent only splits tasks, schedules, and accepts results. The coder writes code, the writer writes documentation, and the reviewer reviews. Each subagent receives only the context for its own domain. The key difference is **asynchrony**. In TUI mode, after dispatch the main agent **immediately returns a receipt** (`Dispatched <agent>. taskId: <taskId>`). The subagent runs in the background, and when it finishes, the result is pushed back into the conversation as a **[subagent-result] system notification**. The main agent is not blocked, so it can dispatch multiple tasks in parallel and keep working on other things.

The core of Legion Mode comes down to one thing: write “who can dispatch whom” into a roster, so the whole graph forms a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

HWPX is a format that stores XML (OWPML) inside a ZIP, so you can work with it using only Python, without Hancom Office.
python-hwpx runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, and CI alike, and its only dependency is `lxml`. HWP 5.0 (`.hwp`) files open with the same API and can be converted to HWPX.

```bash
pip install python-hwpx      # Python 3.10+

from hwpx import HwpxDocument

chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.description: Daily football match analysis for Jingcai (China sports lottery), interpreting handicap line movements for football betting
chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.body:
> **Set emotions aside, look only at the signals.**
> Three-channel handicap movement cross-validation: no bets at low odds, no entry when signals are unclear. Automatically executed before kickoff, automatically settled after the match.

## 🚀 Live Site

- **[https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/](https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/)**
- Updated automatically every hour, historical dates archived, available for review anytime
- Covers **500~1300+** matches per day (full Jingcai/Asian handicap coverage), automatically flags signals and bets

---

## The Detours We Bypassed

We tried **models**: piled on parameters until the room was full. Looking back, the model merely recited the prices the market had already set. No matter how many parameters, it couldn't produce anything new.

We tried **studying the bookmakers**: guessing at the house's moves, the more we guessed, the more it looked like paranoid delusion. In the end it became clear: guessing at the bookmaker is less useful than watching the price.

We also tried **AI predictions**: injuries, motivation, form. Each point sounded convincing, and each had long been priced into the odds. No matter how lively the talk, the handicap doesn't accept it.

After the detours, one plain truth remains:

> **Money shows where it's going, and the handicap speaks.**
> But people watching the lines get carried away easily: chasing favorites, fearing upsets, shaky hands at the last minute. You can tell at a glance that emotion is doing the trading.

So we hand both "watching" and "betting" to the machine, and keep only one thing for humans: **discipline**.

## Three Informants, One Referee

**European odds** track market-wide odds movements: who is being collectively abandoned, who is quietly defending, whether the draw defense has been given up. This is the informant closest to the action.

**Asian handicap** tracks lines and water levels: sudden last-minute pivots, sniping by money on the favored side. Money slammed down in real cash is more honest than what people say.

**Over/under** tracks total goal lines: once a breeding ground for goals appears, the number of goals in the match is often already foreshadowed.

Each informant has its own news. When the news lines up, the referee dares to make the call. **Matches where the informants disagree (European odds and Asian handicap contradicting each other) are left alone entirely.** When the informants themselves are arguing, why bet at all?

## Discipline Matters More Than Vision

Once the direction is set, everything else is discipline:

- **No entry at low odds**: single-option odds below 1.5, or double-option odds that discount below 1.3. Even a strong signal isn't bought. At odds that low, even a win doesn't earn much.
- **No entry when signals are unclear**: no signal, conflicting signals, or an ambiguous direction means waiting and watching. Missing out doesn't lose money; betting wrong does.
- **Quality determines stake size**: the stronger the signal, the larger the stake (1/2/4 units). No all-in gambling.
- **Auto-bet 15 minutes before kickoff, auto-settle when results come in**: no last-minute shaky hands, no urge to add stakes after a win or chase losses after a loss.

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

This project is for data research only and does not constitute any purchase advice. Buy lottery tickets only at offline physical stores. Persons under 18 years old may not participate.

# dsh-context-truth

[English](https://github.com/deepseekv41flash/dsh-context-truth/blob/HEAD/README-en.md) · [Simplified Chinese](https://github.com/deepseekv41flash/dsh-context-truth/blob/HEAD/README.md)

> Let the model know its **actual** context occupancy: the host measures it and backfills it every turn, and the false claim "context is nearly used up" is kept from being passed down through compaction summaries.

DSH (DeepSeek Harness) plugin · single peer dependency (the host-bundled `schemastery`) · requires host services `tokenMeter` and `compaction` (included in the standard `dsh-base` deployment) · handoff mode adds 1 tool (`handoff_ready`) · 1 client settings card · no build step · MIT

---

## What problem it solves

**DSH never tells the model its token usage.** The model can only guess from "this session feels long," so in a long session it may declare "the context is running out" at a real occupancy of **17%**, stop write operations, and hand work off to subagents.

Worse, this false judgment **survives compaction**:

1. The model writes "my context is nearly used up";
2. That sentence enters the compaction summary (one measured session summary reads: `- Session budget is nearly exhausted; ...`);
3. The checkpoint's fixed lead-in is *"Treat the captured context as **established background**"*;
4. So each compaction re-injects this false belief as established background, and it **is never corrected even when the real occupancy drops**.

This plugin cuts both ends of this chain.

A dynamic runtime-context line, rendered each turn by the host's own token meter:

you work. This host-measured line is the only…

# Xuanji

> **OpenAI / Anthropic Protocol Aggregation · Load Balancing · Routing Gateway**  
> *Go ecosystem · Single binary · Zero external dependencies · Lightweight alternative to one-api / LiteLLM*

Xuanji (the first star of the Big Dipper, the pivot of ancient astronomical instruments): gathers all directions and turns them into routing.  
A lightweight AI gateway built in Go, providing a unified entry point for AI tools such as Hermes, Claude Code, and OpenCode. It aggregates multiple upstream providers (SiliconFlow, SenseTime, DeepSeek-family relays, vLLM, OpenRouter, etc.) and automatically routes traffic based on cost and health status.

**It is a lightweight alternative to gateways such as one-api / new-api / LiteLLM / Portkey / Kong AI Gateway**: it solves the same problems of a unified entry point for multiple upstreams, API key management, cost control, and failover, but its footprint, dependencies, and deployment cost are an order of magnitude lower. It is also a **server-side alternative to desktop configuration switchers like CC Switch**: no switching is needed, because the gateway schedules automatically.

> **🎯 Positioning: personal / small-team self-use**. It has no billing, user management, quota, or redemption-code operations features, and none are planned in the near term. It is meant to be a unified entry point and cost scheduler for your own AI workflows, not a multi-user billing and distribution system. Usage statistics per API key (request count / tokens / success rate) can help you see which AI programs use the most.

tibidefengzi/ComfyUI-AD-Segmented-Loop.body:
# AD-Segmented Loop · ComfyUI-AD-Segmented-Loop

An asset timeline and segmented loop plugin for ComfyUI. It connects asset preparation, per-segment generation, preview comparison, and result saving into one workflow, suitable for segmented long-video generation, latent bridge continuation, and shot-level redo.

## Four Core Nodes

1. **AD-Asset Preparation**: Batch import and drag-and-drop of images, videos, and audio. Video and audio each have a 3-track timeline supporting dragging, trimming, cutting, splicing, merging, multi-select group move, and undo/redo. Supports smart splitting by section, beat, shot, or breath pause. Outputs per-segment reference images, reference video frames, reference video audio, reference audio, source video/source audio, start frames, and mask-dedicated frames.
2. **AD-Segment Generation**: Organizes segments by asset duration or segment count, strictly locks to 24 FPS, and adapts to H3's 17k+5 generation frame count. Controls width, height, prompts, reference assets, and reference ranges per segment. Built-in latent bridge continuation (including re-anchoring, seam exposure transition, and quality correction).
3. **AD-Segment Preview**: Per-segment playback, A/B comparison, re-rolls for a chosen segment, stop-and-standby with breakpoint resume, continuous segment looping, clip merging, and history round viewing with loop playback. Connects to the finished output of this segment, then continues to approve the next segment.
4. **AD-Final Save**: Batch “Process Selected / Continue Remaining” for externally processed results, with automatic archiving, clip merging, source/finished A/B comparison, and master download. Supports master quality (near-lossless 4:4:4 CRF14, etc.).

Full-graph runs end at **AD-Segment Preview**. Clicking the run button on a preview node limits execution to that preview and its required upstream dependencies. Native partial runs follow the selected target node. After selecting image, audio, or video results in the preview, click “Process Selected” in AD-Final Save to execute the corresponding processing branch.

Native partial runs are compatible with a connected downstream “Display Any GH” node. When a preparation task fails, the specific reason is shown.

## Typical Wiring

```
AD-Asset Preparation ──reference assets / segment list──▶ AD-Segment Generation (external: H3 conditioning / sampling / decoding)
        │                                                        │
        └──preview media / context──▶ AD-Segment Preview ◀───────┘
                                             │
                                             └──results──▶ AD-Final Save
```

- The segment node's `context` connects to the preview node, and the preview node's `media` connects to this segment's `CreateVideo` output.
- The reference image, reference video, reference video audio, and reference audio ports of Asset Preparation connect to the corresponding H3 reference inputs. The mask-dedicated port can connect to SAM/VAEEncode for local inpainting.
- H3's model, conditioning encoding, sampler, and decoding are connected in the external workflow. The installation package does not include models.

## Main Features

- **Multi-asset import**: Images, videos, and audio are managed together, with batch loading and drag-and-drop import. H3's single-pass reference output is still images 10, videos 3, and audio 3.

# ippon-slides

**One message per slide.** A CLI that builds slides from Markdown.

- Black background, large text, and a fade-in on slide transitions
- Output is a **single HTML file** with all CSS and JS included, so it opens offline at the venue
- `--pdf` also outputs a **PDF** in 16:9
- No dependencies

📚 Detailed documentation is in [`docs/`](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/README.md) ([syntax](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/syntax.md) ・ [`::http::`](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/http.md) ・ [`ippon serve`](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/serve.md) ・ [presenter view](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/presenter.md) ・ [theming](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/theming.md) ・ [CLI](https://github.com/under18dev/ippon-slides/blob/HEAD/docs/cli.md)).

## Philosophy: why "ippon"?

The name **ippon (一本)** comes from the judo term for a decisive winning point. One slide decides one message. That is all there is to ippon-slides.

- **One message per slide ([Takahashi method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takahashi_method)).** A slide is not reading material. It is a signal that gets across in an instant. So the text is large and the words are few. The audience should be watching **you**, not the screen, and slides should stay out of the way of your talk and only support it. If you feel the urge to cram in bullet points, that is a sign the slide should be split.
- **The tool disappears, and only the message remains.** The output is a **single HTML file** with all CSS and JS included. …
